---
title: "Performance"
---

phplyr's functions call one or two methods of the table they are given, so
the backend determines how fast a pipeline runs.

## Choosing a backend

- **In-memory `DataFrame`** suits data that fits in memory. Expression
  arguments such as `mean('x')` let phibble compute a grouped summary in one
  pass, without building a table per group as a closure does.
- **A database table (`Phibble\tbl()`)** avoids loading the data into PHP.
  With expressions, `filter()` and `summarise()` run in the database, and only
  the result reaches PHP.
- **Pipelines that return every row** (`mutate()`, `arrange()`, unfiltered
  joins) spend most of their database time transferring rows to PHP.
- **Closures on a database table** load all rows first and then run in
  memory. Use `col()` expressions and phplyr's helpers to keep the work in
  SQL.
- **SQLite columns need declared types.** PDO binds values as strings. In an
  untyped column, SQLite stores them as text and compares numbers as text.
- **PolarsTable** (phibble's Polars backend, on the phpolars extension) runs
  expressions in Polars. A closure step converts the data to a DataFrame and
  back. `PolarsTable::fromPolars(Phpolars\read_csv($path))` skips phibble's
  CSV parse.

## Benchmarks

| Script | Measures |
| --- | --- |
| `bench/harness.php` | phibble's shared workloads on DataFrame, SQLite, and PolarsTable, each as a phplyr pipeline and as direct table calls |
| `bench/backends.php` | Three pipelines on DataFrame, PolarsTable, and SQLite, checking that all return the same rows |
| `bench/backends.R` | Two of those pipelines with dplyr, checking row counts and column sums against phplyr's |
| `bench/models.php` | `lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and `glmer()` on the phit extension and phit-polyfill, one fresh process per run |

Each reports the median of seven runs and lists every run.
`bench/generate.php` writes the harness data with phibble's generator and
seed.
